industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, because the industry is split by the rotation itself: the AI capital-spending theme flipped from leadership to liability this week (Garran, MacroStrategy, 20-Nov; Mark Wilson, Goldman, 20-Nov; Menon, Jefferies, 26-Nov; surplus evidence in GPU rental prices cut by a third, halted shipments and banks selling AI loans), while Goldman's Jaisson (20-Nov) favours Technology among Cyclicals and Morgan Stanley (23-Nov) keeps Adyen Overweight. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). The sector rows carry the view: Semiconductors D, Hardware D (from C this week), Software B2B Enterprise C, Fintech D. Counter-case for D: the industry is the epicentre of the correction; for B: Menon says early estimate cuts bring the semiconductor bottom forward and equipment re-rates first. To D on a hyperscaler guide cut read in the sources.

sector.why: Underweight, carried; the conditions for Neutral (the AI credit channel read stable, or a second house joining Jefferies' European call) are not met: the credit channel was read and is widening (banks selling AI loans, SoftBank CDS 516 basis points), while Menon (Jefferies, 26-Nov) says the cycle peaks around November 2026, troughs no earlier than the first half of 2028, and equipment re-rates first after the first estimate cut. Relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior). No Pool name this week. Counter-case for F: Garran's Cisco analogy and the tape; for C: Menon's 'early cuts bring the bottom forward' and Jaisson favouring Technology. To C when the credit channel is read stable for two weeks or the first Asian estimate cuts are read; to F on a hyperscaler guide cut read in the sources.

geography.why: Overweight, carried: the 15% inclusive US tariff on Switzerland is 'largely as expected' (Goldman, 25-Nov), Roche is Kepler's pharma top pick and 'the clear AI leader in pharma' (26-Nov), and the Swiss market's low-beta character is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank and the franc were not read. Counter-case: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.
